skill.name: baml-integration
skill.description: Guide for type-safe BAML integrations, including schema design, DTO generation, client synchronization, wrappers, retries, caching, and cross-language code generation.
skill.summary: Design and maintain type-safe BAML schemas and generated clients for Python and TypeScript.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: All 80 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, fixed imports, benign identifiers, or constrained maintenance commands. Three medium-risk examples remain: mutable CI dependencies, raw exception disclosure, and unbounded in-memory caches. No audit-directed prompt injection, credential theft, or malicious command intent was found.

remediation.issue: The CI example uses a mutable action tag and installs baml-cli without a version pin.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the action to a reviewed commit and baml-cli to a reviewed version with hashes.

remediation.issue: The FastAPI example returns raw exception text.
remediation.suggestion: Log full errors server-side and return a stable generic message with a correlation identifier.

remediation.issue: The wrapper examples use caches without limits or expiration.
remediation.suggestion: Use bounded caches with expiration, entry size limits, and explicit invalidation.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable CI Dependencies
semantic_findings.description: The CI example uses a mutable action tag and installs baml-cli without a version pin, allowing upstream changes to execute in the workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 217 and 220 use a mutable action tag and an unversioned package install. Both are clear supply-chain exposures, although neither dependency is shown as malicious.

semantic_findings.title: Raw Exception Details Exposed to API Clients
semantic_findings.description: The FastAPI example returns raw exception text, which can reveal provider messages, internal details, or sensitive request context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 383 directly places str(e) in an HTTP 500 response. The exact disclosed data depends on runtime exceptions, but the exposure path is explicit.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded In-Memory Response Cache
semantic_findings.description: The wrappers cache request-derived keys and responses without limits or eviction, so repeated unique inputs can exhaust process memory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both wrapper examples use process-local maps and insert responses without size or age controls. Unique request inputs can therefore grow memory use continuously.

content.value_statement: Unstructured LLM outputs create fragile integrations and repeated parsing work. This skill guides BAML schema design, client generation, synchronization, and wrapper implementation.
actual_capabilities: Inspects existing BAML files, generated clients, and generator configuration.
Designs classes, enums, unions, and typed request and response models.
Guides Python and TypeScript client generation with the BAML CLI.
Aligns BAML types with database models, API contracts, and frontend types.
Provides wrapper patterns for retries, caching, rate limits, fallbacks, metrics, and structured errors.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples, not an executable integration package.
BAML and the required model providers must be installed and configured separately.
Generic examples require adaptation to project schemas, frameworks, and deployment controls.
Type-safe output does not prevent prompt injection, and field descriptions do not replace runtime validation.

use_cases.title: Add a Typed LLM Feature
use_cases.description: Define clear BAML inputs and outputs, generate a client, and connect the function to a backend service.

use_cases.title: Synchronize Application Schemas
use_cases.description: Compare BAML types with database and API models, then plan compatible schema updates and client regeneration.

use_cases.title: Share Types Across the Stack
use_cases.description: Generate Python and TypeScript DTOs that keep service and frontend contracts aligned.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Existing Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this repository for BAML sources, generator configuration, and generated clients. Summarize the current setup and identify missing prerequisites. Do not modify files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an unfamiliar BAML project

prompt_templates.title: Design a Typed Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Design BAML input and output types for [feature]. Reuse existing types where suitable. Include field descriptions, error variants, and the client generation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a new typed LLM feature

prompt_templates.title: Plan Schema Synchronization
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the BAML schema with [database or API models]. List mismatches, compatibility risks, migration order, consumer updates, and client regeneration checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate a schema change across services

prompt_templates.title: Build a Production Wrapper
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement a BAML client wrapper for [language and framework]. Include bounded caching, retries, rate limits, sanitized errors, metrics, dependency injection, and focused tests.

output_examples.input: Review an existing Python service before adding a BAML function.
output: Detected the BAML source directory and generated Python client.
Identified reusable request, response, and enum types.
Recommended one typed function and a client regeneration step.

output_examples.input: Compare an updated database model with the current BAML schema.
output: Found two missing fields and one incompatible numeric type.
Proposed optional fields first to preserve compatibility.
Listed regeneration, consumer updates, and CI verification in order.

output_examples.input: Design a reliable TypeScript wrapper for a generated BAML client.
output: Specified retry limits, sanitized errors, and request metrics.
Recommended a bounded cache with expiration.
Outlined tests for success, timeout, fallback, and cache behavior.

best_practices: Review existing schemas before adding types or functions.
Regenerate clients after every BAML change and verify the generated diff.
Validate external inputs and sanitize errors at application boundaries.
anti_patterns: Do not parse structured model output manually when a BAML type can represent it.
Do not edit generated clients directly because regeneration will overwrite changes.
Do not use unbounded caches or expose raw provider errors in production wrappers.

faq.question: What is BAML?
faq.answer: BAML defines typed LLM functions and generates clients that return structured Python and TypeScript values.

faq.question: Does this skill install BAML?
faq.answer: No. It provides integration guidance. Install and configure the BAML toolchain and model providers separately.

faq.question: Which languages does the skill cover?
faq.answer: The examples focus on generated Python and TypeScript clients.

faq.question: Can it help generate DTOs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains request, response, nested, union, enum, and migration patterns for generated DTOs.

faq.question: Does it support a specific web framework?
faq.answer: The guidance is framework-neutral, with selected FastAPI and frontend integration examples.

faq.question: Do field descriptions enforce validation?
faq.answer: No. Descriptions guide model output. Use runtime validators for strict application constraints.
